newsitem.title: USA: U.S. venture funding hit record $10.1 bln in 1996.
newsitem.headline: U.S. venture funding hit record $10.1 bln in 1996.

text.p: Venture capital firms invested a record $10.1 billion in 1996, as venture funding of small startup companies rose 52 percent from record 1995 levels, according to a study by Coopers and Lybrand LLP.
The accounting firm said on Wednesday that its Money Tree Survey found venture capital firms participated in 2,163 deals in 1996, 40 percent more than were funded in the previous year.
The average size of deals financed rose to $4.7 million last year from $4.3 million in 1995.

"The fourth quarter of 1996 continued to show strong momentum in venture capital investing," said Coopers & Lybrand, noting 571 deals worth $2.6 billion were completed in the fourth quarter, up from $2.3 billion in the third when the July stock market setback cooled deal-making.

James Atwell, who heads Coopers & Lybrand's San Jose, California-based venture capital group, said in releasing the study that the hot initial public offering market of 1996 helped venture investors produce significant returns.
"There's every indication that this trend will continue into 1997," said Atwell, noting that venture partnerships have raised record levels of capital for the past three years.

Atwell cited an abundance of startup Internet companies and networking and communications operations, along with consolidation in the health care sector as factors which helped fuel many of the deals.

Venture capital firms, many of which are based in the Palo Alto-Menlo Park area of California, invest in small emerging companies which are expected to produce rapid growth and returns for the investment and endowment funds, companies and wealthy individuals who bankroll venture funding.

California accounted for the major portion of venture funding commitments in 1996, with deals worth $3.2 billion, up 49 percent from the previous year, while Massachusetts was second and nearly doubled to more than $1 billion.
Texas was third with $596 million, followed by Colorado with $393 million and Florida with $376 million.

Technology-based companies received about 60 percent of total venture capital investment in 1996, with software companies alone accounting for 16 percent of the total value invested, a rise of 112 percent from 1995 levels.
Communications companies were nearly even with software, rising 50 percent to $1.6 billion, and health care investments rose 104 percent to $1.1 billion.

In the fourth quarter, California accounted for $803 million, or 31 percent of investment dollars, followed by Massachusets and Texas. Communications investments of $496 million in the fourth quarter was the top sector with 20 percent of the quarter's investment dollars.
